rationale: Scope is the existing tests tree plus the gates that judge it; no production code change is required to verify or execute consolidation. Evidence confirms the hypothesis is plausible but bounded: 17,426 test() calls across 1,791 files with a mean of only 2.26 expect() per test and median 6 tests/file (p25=3) — a long tail of single-purpose tests. Merge candidates concentrate in schema/pass-through suites: 279 schemaValidates() calls in 59 files, e.g. tests/tools/work-item-tools.test.ts runs separate tests for tool structure, schema acceptance, and provider call-through that each rebuild createMockProvider(). The consolidated multi-assert style already exists in-repo (tests/analytics/intent-classifier.test.ts asserts 10 values in one test), proving the pattern is viable; counter-evidence is scenario-heavy files (tests/opencode-agent/orchestrator.test.ts, 282 tests) where merging would destroy failure diagnostics, and tests/CLAUDE.md's 'do not rewrite stable tests unless the work touches that area' rule. Any consolidation must re-clear the Stryker mutation ratchet (scripts/mutation/baseline.json scores are keyed on test bytes), both coverage floors, and must overturn the prior openspec/changes/lighter-unit-tests-under-load decision that made 'lowering test count or the coverage floor' an explicit non-goal. cross_module=true because candidate suites span tests/tools, tests/analytics, tests/plugins, tests/opencode-agent and shared helpers; no DB migrations, provider-surface changes, or credential handling are implicated; novelty is existing-modules.
